name: Vertical-dewar Q0 versus accelerating-gradient qualification of bare 1.3 GHz niobium SRF cavities in a 2 K helium bath
plain_name: Check how well a bare accelerator cavity stores energy as its field is raised, in a 2 K helium bath
description: Acceptance test of bare (undressed) superconducting RF cavities in a below-grade vertical dewar: the cavity is immersed in liquid helium pumped to 2 K inside a magnetically shielded cryostat and driven with low-power CW RF while the unloaded quality factor Q0 is mapped against accelerating gradient (and against temperature down to ~1.5 K), as done at the Fermilab VTS.
keywords: Check how well a bare accelerator cavity stores energy as its field is raised, in a 2 K helium bath

sources.citation: Design and Commissioning of Fermilab's Vertical Test Stand for ILC SRF Cavities (Ozelis et al., PAC07, WEPMN106)
Initial Results from Fermilab's Vertical Test Stand for SRF Cavities (Ozelis et al., SRF2007, WEP15)

requirements.rationale: Cavities are tested in a nominal 2 K liquid-helium bath.
The cavity is immersed in (pumped) liquid helium; Q0 is measured in the LHe bath.
The RF system must drive and phase-lock to the 1.3 GHz cavity resonance.
Trapped flux degrades Q0, so the cryostat must shield the cavity from ambient field during cool-down (design goal <10 mG).
RF input/pickup cables and instrumentation must pass into the dewar to the cavity.
Full high-power test of a 9-cell cavity used a 500 W CW RF amplifier (needed only for high-gradient runs).
Q versus T sweeps extend below 2 K; the facility operates down to 1.5 K.
